title: A Limiting Satisfiability Threshold for Every Fixed Clause Size
main_claim: For each fixed k>=3, random k-SAT (independent proper uniformly signed k-clauses, sampled with replacement) has a limiting threshold alpha_k in (0,infinity): P_n(floor(cn)) tends to 1 for c<alpha_k and to 0 for c>alpha_k.
coverage:
I read every section of the paper (intro, forcing, concentration, anchors, convergence, three-clause, boundaries) and checked the main proof line by line.
(1) Replacement lemma. I checked q_k = x(b-k+1)/(2(v-k+1)) >= x^{k/(k-1)}/k, the case b<k (x<=1/n<=eps), the bound g*q_k >= 2x when x>eps, and 1-e^{-2x} >= x for x<=1/4.
(2) Integrated forcing. The symmetry reduction to "x_n forced" is correct. Erasing x_n leaves uniform (k-1)-clauses that are independent of B. The implication "forced => B sat and B∧Q unsat" holds. Sequential replacement, done conditionally on everything else, works. The bound P(B∧Q unsat) - P(B unsat) <= Delta + d*eps holds. So do the telescoping bound sum_j Delta_{j,d} <= dg, the Poisson-envelope sum (kM/n)e^{kM/n}g, and the eps term.
(3) Concentration. The martingale deletion bound E D_i^2 <= E Z_i^2 is correct. A_m = {V<m<=V^{-i}}. A_m∩A_l = A_m∩{G_l sat}. The pair bound q_m(1-q_m)^{l-m} is correct, as is q_m <= rho_m^k with min(z,1) <= z^{1/k}. G_m has the law of F_{n,m-1}, so Var = O(n^{1+2/k}). I recomputed the Chebyshev exponents delta_k and eta_k.
(4) Anchors. The first moment at density 2^k and the survival-sum bound are correct. For the Hall deficiency union bound I checked the step (em/t)^t(en/t)^t(t/n)^{kt} <= (e^2 c0 t/n)^t and the o(1) limit.
(5) Poisson interpolation. The add-one derivative formula holds. Killing probabilities are exact even with repeated indices, and the sign follows from convexity with weights n_i/N.
(6) Transfer. The thinning independence via the generating function, n(1-theta_n) <= C(k,2), the e^{-R} lower sandwich, and both Chebyshev transfer directions (including the cap/rounding argument) are correct.
(7) Size comparisons. The choice c = min - 2u^{-delta} is admissible at both sizes because u^{-delta} >= r^{-delta}, s^{-delta}. The neighbour step via s_1(c) >= e^{-c} is correct.
(8) Balanced-tree lemma. q >= s > t gives nonnegative block counts. The child ratio is <= 2(1+1/s) <= 3, children have >= a/3 blocks, a_{j+1} >= 1.5 a_j, the geometric error sum gives B_beta, and the liminf/limsup conclusion follows.
(9) Final assembly. The choices lambda = L_k, b = 2^k+1 < L_k and D = L_k satisfy the theorem's hypotheses.
I also spot-checked the k=3 refinements (the q_3 identity, Var(W) <= Var(V) by truncation) and the k=1 remark. The proof is self-contained: it cites Carenini only for priority and analogy, not as a logical input, so there is no circularity with the family-235 companion paper.
sibling_notes: The family-235 sibling "Computing-the-Random-3-SAT-Threshold" (rank 102) was also reported as no_gap_found. This paper uses no lemma from it; the dependence runs only the other way, if at all.
